compiled_state.title: As a developer, the CI llm-review path detects schema-invalid findings and fails loudly when the validator is unavailable
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Description

**What**: Insert a schema validation hook into `dso_ci_review/runner.py` between `merge_findings()` and `_write_output()` that shells out to `validate-review-output.sh`, and fails loudly when the validator is unavailable or returns an unrecognized exit code.

**Why**: This is the walking skeleton of the epic — without detection, no correction or fail-closed behavior is possible. It also makes the CI llm-review path use the same validation rules as local `/dso:review`, restoring single-source-of-truth.

**Scope**:
- IN: subprocess shell-out with explicit 60s timeout; exit-code routing (schema-pass → continue, schema-fail → emit signal for correction handoff, validator-error → fail-loud); stderr diagnostic naming the schema errors when fail-loud; live regression test invoking the validator (not mocked).
- OUT: the correction dispatch itself (S-B); the config key (S-C); the validation-signal run (S-D); doc update (S-E).

## Done Definitions

- When this story is complete, `runner.py` validates merged findings by shelling out to `validate-review-output.sh code-review-dispatch <tmpfile>` with a 60s subprocess timeout, BEFORE `_write_output()` runs
  ← Satisfies: "When CI llm-review produces a finding that violates the schema, the validation step detects it"
- When this story is complete, the validator's exit-code contract is documented and routed: exit 0 → schema-pass (continue); exit 1 (the script's documented schema-fail code) → schema-fail signal handed off to the correction handoff point (S-B integration point); any other non-zero exit, signal termination, ENOENT/EACCES on the validator binary, or subprocess timeout → critical stderr diagnostic + non-zero CI exit (never silently skipped)
  ← Satisfies: "validator missing/non-executable, subprocess times out, or returns an unrecognized exit code → critical stderr diagnostic + non-zero exit — never silently skipped"
- When this story is complete, unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic; at least one regression test in `tests/skills/dso_ci_review/test_runner_smoke.py` invokes `validate-review-output.sh` live (not mocked) to exercise the actual shell contract
  ← Satisfies: "At least one test invokes validate-review-output.sh live (not mocked)"

## Considerations

- [Testing] At least one regression test invokes `validate-review-output.sh` live (not mocked) to exercise the shell contract; other tests may mock subprocess for speed.
- [Reliability] External dependency on `validate-review-output.sh` — must fail-loud, never silently skip.
- [Reliability] Define and document the exit-code contract for `validate-review-output.sh`: 0=schema-pass; 1=schema-fail (route to correction); any other non-zero or signal termination=validator-error (fail-loud per SC4). Distinguish schema-fail (data problem, route to correction) from validator-error (infrastructure problem, fail loud) — collapsing them either short-circuits correction or masks validator bugs as schema failures.
- [Consumer Impact] Before wiring `validate-review-output.sh` into `runner.py`, audit the existing local-review invocation in `write-reviewer-findings.sh` (args, cwd, stdin vs file input, env vars) and ensure `runner.py` invokes the validator identically — divergence between callers would break the single-source-of-truth invariant the epic exists to establish.
- [Performance] 60s subprocess timeout prevents CI hang on large payloads.
- [Maintainability] Document drift-detection via embedded schema hash `214949ee476be6d0`.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
